problem: Existing VLN agents that imagine unseen scenes (future RGB features or object locations) produce transient predictions that are overwritten each step and never integrated into persistent memory, so no long-term episodic simulation is formed.
motivation: Humans navigate unfamiliar places using episodic simulation and episodic memory, imagining rooms and objects from context (e.g. a laundry room next to a bathroom). Agents degrade in unseen environments because they cannot fuse imagined scenes with past experience for later reasoning.
key_idea: SALI keeps a topological memory that mixes real nodes with imagined nodes, generated by a recurrent imagination tree that produces future depth, semantic and RGB images, and fuses imagination scores into real navigable-node scores.
insight: Imagination helps only when stored in persistent memory: imagination-only memory (SR 58) is worse than reality-only (SR 70), while the hybrid reaches SR 82 (Tab. 2). The room-type prior and waypoint model each add SPL (61→64 and 61→66, 71 together), and a dynamic fusion weight beats a fixed one (SPL 71 vs 67). An overly large imagination range (M=2, N̄=8) hurts SPL because agents at different positions imagine the same destination.
method: Real-Imaginary Hybrid Memory: a topological map with visited, current, navigable and imagination nodes; nodes store panoramic RGB, depth and semantics plus ViT/ResNet features; imagination nodes are capped at N̄ and pruned/merged by feature cosine similarity minus position MSE.

Dynamic Action Planning: an LXMERT-style cross-modal transformer with graph-aware self-attention scores navigable and imagination nodes; imagination scores are multiplied by a learned sigmoid gate γ_t and added to the nearest navigable node's score.

Recurrent Imagination Tree: initialized from a length-K history of depth, semantics and positions plus the current RGB; grown iteratively for up to M imagination steps, with results merged back into the memory (cross-correction).

Inpaint model + room-type model: an encoder-decoder (RedNet/ResNet) predicts depth and semantic images from point-cloud-projected structure maps; a room-type classifier reweights semantic codes through a predefined room-object weight dictionary to reduce ambiguity.
SPADE GAN + waypoint model: SPADE generates RGB from the guidance image, semantic image and depth image; a BERT-based waypoint model predicts the next navigable positions (120×12 heatmap plus NMS).

Training: pre-train the multimodal transformer with MLM, MRC, SAP and OG; separately train the four imagination models (CE+L1, hinge GAN+feature-matching+perceptual, MSE heatmap); fine-tune the imagination-node, text and map encoders.

numbers_note: The ablation tables are inconsistent with Table 1 and with each other. Table 2 gives SR 82 / SPL 70 for the full model, Table 3 gives SPL 71, and Tables 4-5 give SR 80 / SPL 71, against SR 82 / SPL 78 in Table 1. Table 1 numbers are reported as printed.
results: SALI gets R2R val-unseen SR 82 / SPL 78 (NE 1.92) and test-unseen SR 79 / SPL 74, beating ScaleVLN (79/70 val, 77/68 test) and Lily (SPL 72 val). On REVERIE it reaches val-unseen SR 58 / RGS 38 / RGSPL 28 and test-unseen SR 56 / RGS 34 / RGSPL 25. The gains are largest on instructions with complex room and object terms.
limitations: The imagination tree with GAN generation is computationally expensive, and training time grows quickly with imagination range (0.54h→2.51h per epoch).
Semantic images depend on a visual classifier, and the room-object weight dictionary is hand-predefined.
Only discrete Matterport3D environments were evaluated; there are no continuous-environment or real-robot experiments, and the ablation numbers are inconsistent with Table 1.
